extracted.intended_audience: academic researchers, journal reviewers, and editors interested in peer review and publishing practices
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evidence-based discussion about how peer review should function, what makes good reviewing practice, and systemic biases to watch for in academic publishing. Includes empirical measures used to assess reviewer behavior and suggested reforms to improve review fairness and quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality control and error detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review should serve as a mechanism for quality control by identifying errors in manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a core function of peer review (Edström et al., Ozkaya): reviewers are expected to detect mistakes and safeguard scientific integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should help improve the methodological rigor of submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A core function: reviewers should suggest methodological enhancements rather than only pointing out flaws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and presentation enhancement
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should help authors improve clarity, organization, and presentation of their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the peer review core functions: focus on readability and communication of results (e.g., editing suggestions, structure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review acts as a check on ethical aspects of research and reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should flag ethical issues, compliance concerns, and problems with research conduct as part of their role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge advancement
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should ultimately contribute to advancing knowledge by ensuring published work is sound and valuable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A core function: the review process should support the dissemination of reliable, useful findings that move the field forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive Feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Feedback should focus on improving the manuscript rather than merely criticizing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Siau, Kulkarni, & El-Omar (2022) recommend constructive comments that help authors revise; avoid purely negative or destructive remarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should respect deadlines to maintain publication efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely reviews are listed as an essential quality — delays harm authors and the scientific process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain strict confidentiality of reviewed materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must not disclose manuscript content or use privileged information; confidentiality is an explicit reviewer obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict Management
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare and avoid conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should disclose conflicts and recuse themselves when appropriate to preserve impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respectful Tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain professional and courteous communication in reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A respectful tone is urged to ensure feedback is received and acted upon constructively; avoid hostile or demeaning language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind review
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementation of double-blind review processes to reduce bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among key reforms: anonymizing authors and reviewers is proposed to mitigate identity-based biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversification of reviewer pools
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase diversity among reviewers to reduce systemic biases and broaden perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reform recommendation: diversify reviewers by geography, gender, career stage, and background to improve fairness and inclusivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training programs for new reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide training to incoming reviewers to raise review quality and consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal training programs are suggested as a reform to ensure reviewers understand good practices and ethical standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition systems for quality reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: Create systems to recognize and reward high-quality reviewing work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognition (e.g., credit, certificates, incentives) is proposed to motivate thorough, timely, and constructive reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open peer review models for transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt open peer review options to increase transparency of the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open review (e.g., signed reviews, published review reports) is discussed as a reform to hold reviewers accountable and increase trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissive feedback (labeling research 'too niche' or 'not of general interest')
rubrics_metrics.description: A pattern where reviewers dismiss work as 'too niche' or irrelevant to general audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified in qualitative research with LGBTQ+ scholars as a form of gatekeeping; reviewers should avoid dismissing topics due to perceived lack of broad appeal, which can marginalize important perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linguistic barriers
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism focused on authors' language proficiency rather than substantive content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flagged as a bias that punishes non-native speakers; reviewers should distinguish language editing needs from scientific merit and offer constructive language-related suggestions if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heteronormative biases
rubrics_metrics.description: Assumptions or standards that marginalize LGBTQ+ perspectives in review judgments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualitative findings show reviewers may apply heteronormative frames that disadvantage work addressing marginalized identities; reviewers should be aware of and avoid such biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eurocentric standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Preference for Western methodologies and frameworks that can disadvantage non-Western scholarship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should recognize diverse valid methodologies and epistemologies and avoid imposing Eurocentric norms as the sole standard of quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical measures for reviewer harshness
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitative indicators used to assess reviewer negativity and style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Worsham et al. (2022) measured total word count, frequency of positive phrases, frequency of negative phrases, number of question marks (inquiry vs. criticism), and use of polite language (specifically the word 'please'); their analysis found no significant difference for 'Reviewer 2' vs other reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepting reviewer duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The obligation and importance of accepting reviewer assignments to sustain the scientific community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per Prpić et al. (2025): accepting review duties is crucial for community health, but must be balanced with efforts to address systemic bias and improve review quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure feedback is constructive, unbiased, and advances knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Feedback should be critical but framed to improve work, free from bias, and oriented toward advancing the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conclusion emphasizes reframing away from vilifying individual reviewers and focusing on ensuring critique is constructive, unbiased, and serves the goal of knowledge advancement.
